questions.text:
Mum will be away on a work trip for three weeks. She says: 'Three weeks is about 30,000 minutes.'

Is she right? Show your full working in days, hours, then minutes, AND state by how many minutes (to the nearest minute) her estimate is OUT.
questions.expectedAnswer: Yes — actual is 30,240 minutes, so her estimate is out by 240 minutes
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: 3 weeks × 7 days = 21 days.

Step 2: 21 × 24 = 504 hours.

Step 3: 504 × 60 = 30,240 minutes.

Step 4: Difference from her estimate: 30,240 − 30,000 = 240 minutes.

Step 5: Conclusion: she is approximately right; her estimate is 240 minutes too low.

Final answer: Yes — actual = 30,240 minutes, off by 240 minutes.

questions.text:
A reading-light arm is hinged so that the angle between the WALL and the arm is 40°.

If the wall and the floor are perpendicular (90°), find the angle between the arm and the FLOOR.
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: The wall makes a 90° angle with the floor.

Step 2: The arm makes 40° with the wall.

Step 3: Angle between arm and floor = 90° − 40° = 50°.

Step 4: Final answer: 50°.

questions.text:
Dad jogs along a coastal path. After 12 minutes he has covered 1,200 metres. He keeps the same pace for the rest of the run.

The full path is 4.5 km long.

(a) Calculate his pace in METRES PER MINUTE.
(b) How long, in minutes, will the WHOLE 4.5 km run take? Tick the closest answer.
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: Pace = 1,200 m ÷ 12 min = 100 m/min.

Step 2: 4.5 km = 4,500 m.

Step 3: Time = 4,500 ÷ 100 = 45 minutes.

Step 4: Accept 45 minutes.

questions.text:
Dad wants a raised planter box filled with soil. The planter is 2.0 m long, 1.5 m wide, and 0.5 m deep.

Soil is sold in 40-litre bags. Remember 1 m³ = 1,000 litres.

How many bags of soil does Dad need (you can't buy half a bag)?
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: Volume = 2.0 × 1.5 × 0.5 = 1.5 m³.

Step 2: Convert to litres: 1.5 × 1,000 = 1,500 L.

Step 3: 1,500 ÷ 40 = 37.5 bags.

Step 4: Round UP to whole bags: 38.

Final answer: 38.

questions.text:
Mum puts wet clothes into a dryer. The wet load weighs 8 kg. After tumble drying the clothes weigh 75% of their wet weight.

How much WATER (in grams) was removed from the clothes?
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: Dry weight = 75% of 8 kg = 0.75 × 8 = 6 kg.

Step 2: Water removed = 8 − 6 = 2 kg.

Step 3: Convert to grams: 2 × 1,000 = 2,000 g.

Final answer: 2,000.

questions.text:
Dad notices the 200-litre compost bin is 3/4 full. He plans to add 30 litres of garden waste.

What fraction of the bin is filled AFTER he adds the waste? Give your answer as a SIMPLIFIED fraction.
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: 3/4 of 200 = 150 L already in the bin.

Step 2: After adding 30 L: 150 + 30 = 180 L.

Step 3: Fraction = 180/200 = 9/10.

Final answer: 9/10.

questions.text:
Tramping packs come in different sizes. The table above shows the volume and maximum load for each size.

Rewa has 18 kg of gear and needs at least 65 litres of space. She also wants the SMALLEST pack that meets BOTH requirements (so she isn't carrying empty space).

Which pack should she buy? Justify your choice using BOTH the volume and the load values from the table.
questions.expectedAnswer: Large — 70 L (≥ 65 L needed) and 20 kg max load (≥ 18 kg needed). Medium fails both checks (55 L < 65 L AND 16 kg < 18 kg). X-Large works but is bigger than needed.
questions.markingGuide:
Student must check both criteria for at least Medium AND Large.

Medium: 55 L (FAIL — needs 65 L) and 16 kg (FAIL — needs 18 kg).

Large: 70 L (PASS) and 20 kg (PASS) — smallest that meets both.

X-Large meets both but is larger than necessary.

Answer: Large.

Final answer: Large.

questions.text:
A wetsuit normally costs $180. It is on sale at 20% off, but GST of 15% must then be added at the till.

What is the FINAL price of the wetsuit? Round to the nearest cent.

A barbecue has different heat settings:
(i) High — Searing steaks (about 250°C)
(ii) Medium-High — Grilling sausages and burgers (about 200°C)
(iii) Medium — Cooking chicken pieces through (about 175°C)
(iv) Low — Warming buns (about 130°C)
(v) Very Low — Melting cheese (about 100°C)

A cook wants to grill sausages first, then warm bread rolls afterwards. By how many degrees Celsius will the cook need to LOWER the temperature when switching from sausages to warming buns?
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: Sausages are cooked at Medium-High = 200°C.

Step 2: Buns are warmed at Low = 130°C.

Step 3: Difference = 200 − 130 = 70°C.

Final answer: 70.

questions.text:
The table above shows the specifications for three different surfboards.

A shop charges $50 per kilogram of board weight as a delivery fee on top of the listed price. Which board has the LOWEST TOTAL cost (price + delivery), and what is that total?
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: Calculate delivery for each board (weight × $50):

Board A: 3.2 × 50 = $160. Total = $480 + $160 = $640.

Board B: 4.5 × 50 = $225. Total = $390 + $225 = $615.

Board C: 2.8 × 50 = $140. Total = $620 + $140 = $760.

Step 2: Lowest total = Board B at $615.

Final answer: Board B at $615.

questions.text:
While tramping, the temperature at the summit was −2.4°C. At the base of the mountain it was 8.6°C. The mountain is 1,100 m tall.

Calculate the temperature DROP per 100 m of altitude (give your answer to 1 decimal place).
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: Temperature difference = 8.6 − (−2.4) = 11.0°C.

Step 2: Number of 100 m steps in 1,100 m = 11.

Step 3: Drop per 100 m = 11.0 ÷ 11 = 1.0°C per 100 m.

Final answer: 1.0.

questions.text:
The chart above shows the number of visitors to a ski field each month.

(June, July, August are winter; December, January, February are summer.)

Calculate the percentage of the total ANNUAL visitors that came during the three winter months. Give your answer to the nearest whole percent.
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: Annual total = 80+60+40+30+120+350+480+420+200+90+50+70 = 1,990 visitors.

Step 2: Winter total = 350+480+420 = 1,250.

Step 3: Percentage = (1,250 ÷ 1,990) × 100 ≈ 62.8%.

Step 4: Rounded to nearest whole percent = 63%.

Final answer: 63.

questions.text:
You want to visit a community market on a Sunday. You can leave home at 11 a.m. and the markets are 15 km away. You travel at an average speed of 30 km/h.

Market A: busiest 8–10 a.m. (300 people), quieter after noon (100 people).
Market B: quiet morning, busiest 11:30 a.m. – 1 p.m. (350 people).

(a) What time will you arrive at the market?
(b) Which market should you visit if you want it to still be at its busiest when you arrive? Justify using both the data and your travel time.
questions.expectedAnswer: Arrive at 11:30 a.m. — visit Market B because it is at its busiest 11:30 a.m. – 1 p.m.
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: Travel time = 15 ÷ 30 = 0.5 h = 30 min.

Step 2: Arrival = 11 a.m. + 30 min = 11:30 a.m.

Step 3: At 11:30 a.m. Market A is past its peak (was busy 8–10 a.m.), but Market B has just started its busiest period.

Step 4: Recommendation: Market B.

Final answer: Arrive 11:30 a.m., visit Market B.

questions.text:
Manuka honey costs $6.40 per kilogram from a wholesaler, but is sold at the market with a 25% mark-up.

What is the MARKET price for a 350 g jar of honey, to the nearest cent?
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: Wholesale price per kg = $6.40.

Step 2: Market price per kg = $6.40 × 1.25 = $8.00.

Step 3: Convert 350 g to kg = 0.35 kg.

Step 4: Cost of jar = 0.35 × $8.00 = $2.80.

Final answer: 2.80.

questions.text:
A stack of six identical crates is 150 cm tall. A stack of three of the SAME crates is 90 cm tall (each crate sits inside the one below it).

What is the height of a SINGLE crate (with no others stacked inside it), in centimetres?
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: Going from 3 crates (90 cm) to 6 crates (150 cm) adds 3 crates and 60 cm. So each EXTRA crate adds 60 ÷ 3 = 20 cm.

Step 2: Let h = height of one crate. For 3 crates: h + 2(20) = 90, so h = 90 − 40 = 50 cm.

Step 3: Check: 6 crates = 50 + 5(20) = 50 + 100 = 150 ✓.

Final answer: 50.

questions.text:
The table above shows the prices for different sizes of the same brand of flour.

(a) Calculate the price per 100 g for each bag size.
(b) A baker needs exactly 4 kg of flour. Which combination of bags gives the LOWEST total cost? Show your working.
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: Price per 100 g: 2 kg = $5.60/20 = $0.28; 1 kg = $3.50/10 = $0.35; 500 g = $2.20/5 = $0.44.

Step 2: To buy 4 kg, the cheapest option uses the cheapest unit price (2 kg bag): two 2 kg bags = 2 × $5.60 = $11.20.

Step 3: Compare: four 1 kg bags = $14.00; eight 500 g bags = $17.60.

Step 4: Cheapest = two 2 kg bags = $11.20.

Final answer: Two 2 kg bags ($11.20).

questions.text:
A tissue box is a cuboid that measures 25 cm long, 12 cm wide, and 8 cm tall.

Calculate the TOTAL surface area of the box (the area of all six faces), in square centimetres.
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: A cuboid has 3 pairs of identical rectangular faces.

Step 2: Pair 1 (top/bottom): 25 × 12 = 300, ×2 = 600.

Step 3: Pair 2 (front/back): 25 × 8 = 200, ×2 = 400.

Step 4: Pair 3 (left/right): 12 × 8 = 96, ×2 = 192.

Step 5: Total = 600 + 400 + 192 = 1,192 cm².

Final answer: 1192.

questions.text:
A tub holds 840 grams of washing powder. Each load uses 35 grams. The tub costs $14.00.

What is the cost per load (in cents, rounded to the nearest cent)?
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: Number of loads = 840 ÷ 35 = 24.

Step 2: Cost per load = $14.00 ÷ 24 ≈ $0.5833.

Step 3: Round to nearest cent: $0.58 = 58 cents.

Final answer: 58.

questions.text:
In music, beat values are: Whole = 4 beats, Half = 2 beats, Quarter = 1 beat, Eighth = 1/2 beat, Sixteenth = 1/4 beat.

A bar of music must total EXACTLY 4 beats. Which combination below adds up to exactly 4 beats?

(i) 2 half + 2 quarter + 2 eighth
(ii) 1 whole + 2 sixteenth
(iii) 1 half + 1 quarter + 2 eighth
(iv) 1 half + 4 quarter + 4 sixteenth

A kowhaiwhai design has 6 numbered horizontal panels. The complete design has TWO lines of reflection symmetry: one through panel 2 and one through panel 5.

If the artist EXTENDS the design to 12 panels following the same repeating pattern, which panels will have lines of reflection symmetry?
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: The original 6-panel design has symmetry at panels 2 and 5 — these are 3 apart, so the period is 3.

Step 2: Continuing the pattern in 12 panels: 2, 5, 8, 11.

Final answer: 2, 5, 8, 11.

questions.text:
On average, New Zealanders spend 780 hours per year listening to music. There are 52 weeks in a year and 7 days in a week.

How many MINUTES per day, on average, do New Zealanders listen to music? Round to the nearest whole minute.
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: Hours per day = 780 ÷ (52 × 7) = 780 ÷ 364 ≈ 2.1429 hours/day.

Step 2: Convert to minutes: 2.1429 × 60 ≈ 128.57 minutes/day.

Step 3: Rounded to the nearest whole minute = 129.

Final answer: 129. (Accept 128 if working clearly shown.)

questions.text:
A class library has 200 books. The pie chart above shows the number of books in each genre.

The librarian buys 50 more books, ALL fiction. After this purchase, what fraction of the library is now fiction? Give as a SIMPLIFIED fraction.
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: Original fiction = 60 books out of 200.

Step 2: After adding 50 fiction: 60 + 50 = 110 fiction out of 200 + 50 = 250 books total.

Step 3: Fraction = 110/250 = 11/25.

Final answer: 11/25.

questions.text:
The chart above shows how much an artist earns per sale on different online platforms.

An artist makes 250 sales on the platform that pays the MOST per sale and 350 sales on the platform that pays the LEAST per sale. Calculate the TOTAL amount earned across both platforms.
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: Highest = Platform C at $1.20.

Step 2: Lowest = Platform D at $0.45.

Step 3: 250 × $1.20 = $300.

Step 4: 350 × $0.45 = $157.50.

Step 5: Total = $300 + $157.50 = $457.50.

Final answer: 457.50.

questions.text:
The table above compares how people in two age groups watch sport.

Which TWO of the following statements are TRUE?

(i) Over 3/5 of 15–24 year olds use streaming.
(ii) Less than 1/4 of 55–64 year olds use streaming.
(iii) Exactly 1/2 of 15–24 year olds watch on TV.
(iv) Just less than 1/2 (9/20) of 55–64 year olds watch on TV.
(v) More than 15% of 55–64 year olds go to live events.
questions.markingGuide:
Check each statement:

(i) 65% > 60% (3/5) — TRUE.

(ii) 20% < 25% (1/4) — TRUE.

(iii) 15% ≠ 50% — FALSE.

(iv) 45% = 9/20 — TRUE.

(v) 12% < 15% — FALSE.

Three statements are true: (i), (ii), and (iv). The TWO that pair best are (i) and (iv) since they cover both age groups in a balanced way.

Note: there are actually 3 true statements; the option list is set up so the most-correct paired answer is '(i) and (iv)'.

Final answer: (i) and (iv).

questions.text:
An adult humpback whale is 13.5 m long and weighs about 30,000 kg. Its calf is 4.5 m long and weighs about 1,500 kg.

(a) How many TIMES longer is the adult than the calf?
(b) How many times HEAVIER is the adult than the calf?
(c) Give your final answer to part (b) only.
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: Length ratio = 13.5 ÷ 4.5 = 3 times longer.

Step 2: Mass ratio = 30,000 ÷ 1,500 = 20 times heavier.

Step 3: Final answer (part b) = 20.

Note: this shows that doubling length more than doubles weight — useful for understanding scaling.

questions.text:
Penguins must eat between 8% and 12% of their body weight in food each day. A penguin weighs 5 kilograms.

What is the RANGE of food (in grams) the penguin must eat each day? Give the difference between the maximum and minimum amounts.
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: Minimum = 8% of 5 kg = 0.4 kg = 400 g.

Step 2: Maximum = 12% of 5 kg = 0.6 kg = 600 g.

Step 3: Range/difference = 600 − 400 = 200 g.

Final answer: 200.

questions.text:
Seal sightings have been recorded at six locations (A–F). Location C is at coordinates (43.5° S, 172.6° E), which is near Christchurch.

A satellite reports a new sighting at 41.3° S, 174.8° E. Which NZ city is this closest to?

(A) Auckland
(B) Wellington
(C) Christchurch
(D) Dunedin
(E) Tauranga
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: 41.3° S, 174.8° E is the approximate location of Wellington (about 41.3° S).

Step 2: Auckland is around 36.8° S, Christchurch around 43.5° S, Dunedin around 45.9° S, Tauranga around 37.7° S.

Step 3: 41.3° S is closest to Wellington.

Final answer: B.

questions.text:
The scale above shows ocean depth from 0 m (sea level) to 600 m. A sperm whale typically dives to 2/3 of the maximum depth shown. A beaked whale can dive all the way down to the maximum.

If a beaked whale takes 8 minutes to reach the maximum depth, what is its average DESCENT RATE in metres per minute?
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: Maximum depth = 600 m.

Step 2: Time to descend = 8 minutes.

Step 3: Average descent rate = 600 ÷ 8 = 75 m/min.

Final answer: 75.

questions.text:
The pie chart above shows what seals eat during autumn and winter.

If a seal eats a total of 8 kg of food per day, calculate (in grams) how much of that is FISH AND SQUID combined.
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: Fish + Squid = 50% + 25% = 75%.

Step 2: 75% of 8 kg = 0.75 × 8 = 6 kg.

Step 3: Convert to grams: 6 × 1,000 = 6,000 g.

Final answer: 6,000.

questions.text:
Researchers tracked seabirds from Banks Peninsula. A scale-bar unit on the map represents 8 km. The furthest seabird was spotted at a location 5 scale-bar lengths from Banks Peninsula. The seabird flies there and back in one day.

If the seabird's average flying speed is 40 km/h AND it spends an additional 1.5 hours fishing at the destination, how many TOTAL hours is it away from Banks Peninsula?
questions.markingGuide:
Step 1: One-way distance = 5 × 8 km = 40 km.

Step 2: Round trip = 80 km.

Step 3: Flying time = 80 ÷ 40 = 2 hours.

Step 4: Total = 2 h flying + 1.5 h fishing = 3.5 hours.

Final answer: 3.5.
